source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of the second topic printed as 2.7.2 (Pauli's exclusion principle), printed page 36.

blocks.title: Pauli ka exclusion principle
blocks.text: Kisi atom mein koi do electrons aise nahi ho sakte jin ke chaaron quantum numbers ki qeematein bilkul ek jaisi hon. Doosre lafzon mein: “ek orbital ke do electrons ke spins hamesha opposite (ulte) hote hain”.
Helium (He) atom ke pehle shell mein do electrons hain, dono 1s orbital mein. Quantum numbers aur Pauli ke principle ke mutabiq un ki qeematein yeh hain:

blocks.caption: Table 2.6 Ek orbital ke do electrons ke quantum numbers

blocks.text: Dono electrons ke ‘n’, ‘ℓ’ aur ‘m’ ek jaise hain, magar ‘s’ alag hai. Matlab un ke spins ulti directions mein hain.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Isi principle ki wajah se ek orbital mein zyada se zyada do electrons aate hain: n, ℓ, m same hon to sirf s badal sakta hai, aur s ki sirf do qeematein (+½, −½) hain.

blocks.prompt: Kya helium ke 1s orbital mein teesra electron aa sakta hai? Principle se jawab dein.
blocks.explanation: Nahi. Teesre electron ke bhi n = 1, ℓ = 0, m = 0 honge, aur s +½ ya −½ hi ho sakta hai, jo pehle do mein se kisi ek ke chaaron numbers dohrayega. Pauli ka principle is ki ijazat nahi deta.

items: Pauli: atom mein koi do electrons chaaron quantum numbers same nahi rakh sakte.
Ek orbital mein zyada se zyada 2 electrons, ulte spins ke saath.
